full_judgment:
7. Mr M Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division has erred in law in reversing the judgment and decree, passed by the appellate Court without adverting to the findings of the appellate Court that Chandra Kanta Saha and Lolit Mohon Saha had in total 0.72½ acre of land in their share of RS Khatian Nos. 27, 40 and 155, which were acquired by Abul Kashem Bepari by pattan. 

 9. Per contra Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. Mr Neogi also submits that the High Court Division while exercising its revisional jurisdiction is competent to reverse the judgment of the Courts below, since the same has been made upon misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence causing failure of justice, as a matter of course, judgment passed by the High Court Division having been in true spirit of laws and principles in exercise of discretionary civil revisional power to do complete justice between the litigant parties for the administration of which also it had been created and the same having been well founded, well grounded and well-reasoned and no illegality and legal infirmity having been manifested, no interference is called for by this Division. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate Court without proper appreciation of the evidence on record and without adverting the findings of the trial Court with regard to title and possession, perfunctorily reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, inasmuch as the rayati settlement (pattan) in favour of the predecessor of the defendants was not substantiated before the trial Court; despite, mere submitting a rent receipt is not sufficient to prove their right and title in the suit land.
